 Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 29 points (9-of-19 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and six three-pointers in a 120-100 win over the Heat on Thursday.
 Despite a rough start to this game, Curry got going in the third quarter. After scoring seven points on 2-of-10 shooting in the first half, he scored 14 points in the third quarter alone and eight more points in the fourth to steal the win for Golden State. Curry has been unbelievable to start the season, which has him ranked as one of the best players in fantasy basketball to this point. He’ll look to stay hot against the Magic to wrap up the week on Saturday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Stephen Curry tallied 34 points (9-of-21 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns. 
 While he didn’t have his best night shooting the basketball, Curry extended his streak of games with at least 31 points to three. The Warriors star was at his best in the third quarter, shooting 6-of-9 from the field and scoring 18 points. Outside that period, the Suns kept Curry in check, but he still went home with a stat line that many fantasy managers will take without hesitation.

 Guard

 Stephen Curry (knee) is out for Sunday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Curry is going to sit out Sunday for right knee injury management reasons. Will Richard is likely the top candidate to move into the starting lineup with Curry sidelined. 
 Stephen Curry 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Stephen Curry finished Friday’s win over the Lakers with 31 points (11-of-23 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and eight three-pointers. 
 The Warriors got off to a terribly slow start, being outscored 38-15 in the first quarter. The bench came up big in the second quarter, setting the stage for Curry to do his usual work in the second half. He scored 17 of his 31 after halftime, helping the Warriors turn a 25-point deficit into a 17-point victory. During the fourth quarter, Curry moved into 18th on the NBA’s all-time scoring list, passing Dominique Wilkins. Over the last two games, he’s scored 75 points and knocked down 14 three-pointers. 
 Stephen Curry 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Stephen Curry with an absolute monster performance with 44 points (11-of-27 FGs, 16-of-16 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists, two steals, and six 3-pointers in 119-114 win against the Timberwolves. 
 Steph can still go crazy in games but it doesn’t happen as often with his age. Getting a perfect 16-16 from the free throw line is an incredible boost to your fantasy teams at this point in the week. As long as he is healthy, he will be one of the most exciting players in the NBA, and you can take any of these performances you can get as a fantasy owner.

 Stephen Curry accounted for 24 points (8-of-8 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets. 
 For just the second time in his illustrious career, Curry finished a game without missing a shot. After making his lone attempt during the first half, the Warriors guard shot 7-of-7 from the field in the second half as they pulled away from the Nuggets. Given Yaxel Lendeborg’s play, the Warriors didn’t have to rely as much on Curry. If that continues, it would make the future Hall of Fame guard’s job a little easier.

 Stephen Curry tallied 24 points (5-of-15 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies. 
 Curry led the Warriors in scoring on Friday, but he shot a frigid 5-of-15 from the field. The assists were solid, but this was not the best night to have the Warriors star in most fantasy lineups. After the game, Curry said he “probably” won’t play against the Suns on Saturday, bad news for fantasy managers hoping for a bounce-back effort.

 Stephen Curry gets 23 points (12-of-19 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, two steals, and two 3-pointers against the Lakers. 
 Curry did what he could to try and keep the Warriors in this game, but it was to no avail. You would want him to have more assists, but his teammates weren’t hitting shots. With no Porzingis for the foreseeable future, there’s a chance that the Warriors will have many more blowouts which will reduce Curry’s minutes.

 Will Richard started on Thursday and finished with 10 points (4-of-6 FGs), one rebound, two assists, one block and two three-pointers against the Heat.
 Richard got the starting nod for the second straight game and for the third time this season. Multiple players have filled out the fifth starting spot with Jimmy Butler III (knee) sidelined to start the year. Richard only played 16 minutes in this game, with Georges Niang and Brandon Williams each surpassing 20 minutes and scoring in double figures. Richard may continue to start, but he isn’t worth adding off the waiver wire.

 Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), two rebounds, eight assists, one steal, four three-pointers and five turnovers in a 120-100 loss to the Warriors on Thursday.
 Mitchell’s breakout season continued in this game as he matched his season high for both points and three-pointers. His assists continue to be the strongest aspect of his game, but he is averaging career highs for points, triples and steals as well while also posting the best shooting percentage of his career. It has been a rough start to the year for Miami, but Mitchell has been able to thrive regardless.

 Ryan Conwell provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (4-of-9 FGs), one rebound, two assists, three steals and three three-pointers against the Warriors on Thursday.
 Conwell entered the rotation on Wednesday, but he wasn’t able to score in the first game that he played over 10 minutes. However, he was able to light it up in this one. The rookie was an elite shooter during his final collegiate season, so it isn’t surprising that he was able to pour in the triples. He’s a depth option for Miami, but he won’t play enough to be worth adding off the waiver wire.

 After having his best performance of the season on Wednesday, Adebayo wasn’t able to provide an encore, though he was able to record his second double-double of the year.  Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, three steals and four three-pointers in a 117-104 win over the Magic on Thursday.
 Booker has had a few rough performances early on this season, but this has been an excellent two-game stretch for him. He has scored at least 30 points in back-to-back games, and he set a new season high for assists, steals and three-pointers in this one. Outside of a dud game against the Thunder, Booker has been excellent this season. He’ll continue to have the ball in his hands, and if he’s shooting the ball this well, the results will continue to be great for fantasy managers.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Miles Bridges stuffed the stat sheet on Thursday with 18 points (6-of-10 FGs), 13 rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers against the Magic.
 With both Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach in foul trouble, Bridges was able to step up on the glass. He ended up setting a new season high for rebounds in what has been an excellent start to the year for him, especially as of late. Over his last four games, Bridges has averaged 20.3 points, 9.0 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 2.3 steals, 1.0 block and 3.0 triples per game while shooting 51.8 percent from the free throw line. He has been fantastic in fantasy basketball and will look to stay hot against the Rockets on Saturday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Dillon Brooks posted a full line on Thursday with 24 points (9-of-16 FGs), one rebound, one assist, two steals, one block and four three-pointers against the Magic.
 Brooks’ scoring has dropped off this season, but he has made up for it with improved efficiency. However, he was able to do both in this game, which led to his best scoring performance of the season. Brooks has shot at least 55 percent from the floor in three of his last four games, which has helped his value in nine-category leagues. He likely won’t continue to shoot this well, but he certainly has the hot hand right now.

 Head coach Jordan Ott made the call to replace Khaman Maluach with Ighodaro in the starting unit. Unfortunately, Ighodaro found himself in foul trouble throughout the game, which prevented him from providing much value. Ighodaro is worth considering as a waiver wire pickup, even if this first game as a starter was rough. He won’t do much scoring, but he’s a strong passer for a big man and has five blocks over his last three games.
